SAMT-BU tests solutions through pilots. A pilot is a bounded, time-limited effort with its own team, its own deliverables and a defined end. This section covers the pilots – what they set out to answer, who takes part and what they have produced.

> **⚠ Working draft as of 28 July 2026.** The overview of pilot candidates below is compiled from the material for the 26 August workshop and has **not been decided**. The compilation is editorial, and the mapping between cases and pilots in particular needs to be quality assured. Input and corrections are welcome.

## Cases and pilots are two different things

It is easy to conflate *cases* and *pilots*, and the project's documents often use the terms interchangeably. The distinction matters:

- A **case** describes a **need** – a situation that does not work well enough today. The cases are found under [Needs](https://docs.samt-bu.no/en/behov/use-cases/).
- A **pilot** is an **implementation measure** – a concrete attempt to do something about one or more needs.

The relationship between them is **many-to-many**. One pilot can address several cases, and one case can be touched by several pilots – fully or partly, at different stages. This also means that:

- **Cases are not merged.** Two cases appearing in the same pilot proposal does not make them one case. Each keeps its own description and is given a relationship instead.
- **Cases do not "lapse" because they are covered elsewhere.** A need handled through a pilot tied to another case is still a real need. "Lapsed" should be reserved for needs that have genuinely been rejected.

> **Note:** The current case register does not apply this distinction consistently – some cases are marked as incorporated into or replaced by others. This will be cleaned up later, together with the work on a more precise metamodel for needs, solutions, goals and deliverables.

## Pilot candidates for the 26 August workshop

New pilots will be selected at the workshop. This time the selection places more weight on **feasibility and the partners' ability to contribute** than on finding the "right" case – the main constraint has been capacity to carry pilots out, not a shortage of good needs.

Eight candidates have been sent to the participants:

| Case | What the pilot proposal is about |
|---|---|
| [2 – Transition from primary to upper secondary](https://docs.samt-bu.no/en/behov/use-cases/02-overgang-grunnskole-vgo/) | Continuation of pilot 1. The pilot showed potential for substantial efficiency gains, but no final decision was made on how the solution should be realised. Solution alternatives are being assessed in the architecture group. |
| [3](https://docs.samt-bu.no/en/behov/use-cases/03-id-haandtering-flyktninger/) and [26](https://docs.samt-bu.no/en/behov/use-cases/26-nasjonal-tjeneste-for-identifikasjon-av-personer-i-utdanning-utdanningspersonregister/) – Identification of persons in education | Handling persons without a national identity number or D-number. Case 3 describes the challenge in the municipal sector, case 26 a sector-wide solution through an education person register. One point of discussion is whether more investigation is needed before going straight to a solution. |
| [6 – Centralised access to the data parents need](https://docs.samt-bu.no/en/behov/use-cases/06-sentralisert-datatilgang/) | Give parents access to national tests, mapping assessments and final assessments in one place. Draws data from many sources and has a clear end-user focus. |
| [7 – Early identification of at-risk pupils](https://docs.samt-bu.no/en/behov/use-cases/07-tidlig-identifisering/) | Scoped to investigating whether an AI-driven prediction model is feasible, and what data is required for it to be accurate enough. |
| [10 – Transition to other municipal services](https://docs.samt-bu.no/en/behov/use-cases/10-overgang-kommunale-tjenester/) | Exchange of data between schools and other municipal services such as child welfare and educational psychology services. |
| [11 – Digital dialogue between kindergarten/school and the home](https://docs.samt-bu.no/en/behov/use-cases/11-digital-dialog-hjem/) | A foundation for better ongoing dialogue with the home. One question is whether the case can be solved through creative use of the supplier market. |
| [25 – National tests and mapping assessments](https://docs.samt-bu.no/en/behov/use-cases/25-nasjonale-proever-og-kartlegginger/) | Give municipalities access to the raw data from national tests also after it is no longer available through the Directorate of Education's portal. |
| [27 – National education register](https://docs.samt-bu.no/en/behov/use-cases/27-nasjonalt-utdanningsregister/) | Part of the work to establish a coherent national infrastructure for collecting and sharing data on education and competence in Norway. |

In addition there is a prepared pilot proposal for [case 22 – Analysis data from kindergarten to adult education](https://docs.samt-bu.no/en/behov/use-cases/22-analysedata-for-hele-l%C3%B8pet/): retrieving data from Statistics Norway and presenting it in a dashboard on KS Digital's data platform, with Asker municipality as a candidate participant.

> **⚠ Unresolved:** The material refers to "9 (8)" cases. The message to participants lists the eight in the table above, while case 22 has its own prepared proposal. Whether case 22 is included as a ninth candidate at the workshop needs to be confirmed.

## Gatherings

| Date | What |
|---|---|
| 5 August 2026 | The case descriptions are sent to all participants, with a request for feedback on whether the content is adequate and for proposed clarifications or changes. |
| 25 August 2026 | All case descriptions are reviewed in the architecture group. |
| 26 August 2026 | Workshop at Gardermoen (3.5 hours). Participants distribute themselves across groups – one per case – and outline how the pilot could be carried out. If no one signs up for a case, it will not be worked on. Results are presented in plenary. |

The groups work on three questions: what the goal of the pilot is in the first three-month cycle, what the pilot should produce (dream journey, information and data models, data products, high-level architecture, solution design, prototypes, frameworks and more), and what competence is needed and how it will be obtained. The most important thing to settle is who will take the lead on each case.
